messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Pager — elevated 5xx rate and outbound jitter observed for inference in us-west-2a. Threshold triggered: 5xx > 10% across inference tier for 3m. Runbook: network/az-egress. Please acknowledge.

maria: acknowledging. seeing spike in 5xx and tail latency on model runner pool rwd-large-1 in us-west-2a.  p50 ~ 120ms -> p95 1.2s, many 502/504s.

aj: I'm oncall. pulling NLB and ENI stats now. tagging this P1 until we confirm blast radius. assigning myself to mitigation.

devon: looking at host metrics, netdev rx/tx counters show bursts of retransmits and RX jitter on several G5 hosts in az1a. Noticing increased kernel drops on ifb qdisc.

samir: running quick traceroute and curl checks from control plane into affected nodes:
```
traceroute to 10.0.34.12 (10.0.34.12), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1 (10.0.0.1)  0.45 ms  0.23 ms  0.24 ms
 2  * * *
 3  100.64.3.5 (100.64.3.5)  12.4 ms !H  15.2 ms !H  12.7 ms !H
```
curl against health endpoint shows intermittent connection reset: `curl -v https://inference-usw2a.internal/health` sometimes returns 500 or times out.

maria: looks like an AZ egress plane issue or host NIC offload degradation. early signal: dns results OK, but outbound path jitter/loss from instances.

aj: starting smart routing fallback to send new inference requests to us-west-2b. reducing DNS TTL to 30s. executing steer: 
```
# internal traffic router CLI (example)
router steer set --scope inference --from-zone us-west-2a --to-zone us-west-2b --pct 100 --reason "az1a outbound jitter"
```
Expect propagation within ~1m; will monitor errors and latency.

devon: note: we should invalidate prefix/KV cache on clients before full cutover to avoid stale sticky sessions. pushing a kvcache flush to runtime: 
```
# invalidate prefix cache for affected pools
/opt/runtime/bin/rwctl cache flush --pool rwd-large-1 --prefix all
```
This will add small overhead but avoid partial requests failing due to sticky routing.

customer-success: flagged top-10 paying customers that had errors. prepping short comms. want to avoid alarmist language — confirming impact buckets.

maria: initial impact estimate: ~7% of total inference requests for the cluster during spike window failed (502/504/timeout). most errors were short (~5-10m window). A handful of customers saw elevated error rates for embeddings and chat.

aj: steering complete. analytics show 95% of traffic moved to us-west-2b within 50s. error rate in us-west-2a now trending down. overall platform 5xx dropped from 12% -> 0.9%. Grafana link: <https://grafana.internal/d/abc123/az-egress>

samir: confirming NLB target health: several targets in az1a were flapping unhealthy. NLB logs show increased TLS handshake timeouts and connection resets originating from host side.

devon: still seeing some kernel retransmit counters elevated on a small set of instances. I’m isolating faulty hosts and will evict pods and cordon. starting drain on g5 hosts with high tx_drop.

maria: agree. cordon + replace instances that show persistent RX/TX anomalies. autoscaling should refill with healthy capacity in us-west-2b.

aj: handoff: I’m passing to devon for cleanup and post-incident follow-up (postmortem owner). Summary for handoff:
- root symptom: outbound packet loss/jitter from subset of hosts in us-west-2a leading to TLS resets and NLB target flaps.
- mitigation: smart routing -> us-west-2b (100%), DNS TTL lowered to 30s, prefix kvcache flush, cordon+drain affected hosts.
- customer impact: ~7% overall error rate spike for ~10m window. limited number of customers had visible failover; CS notified.
- next actions: devon to continue host replacement, collect tcpdump + ENI counters, and own postmortem.

devon: accepted handoff. grabbing tcpdump and ENI metrics now; will escalate to cloud support if hardware path shows persistent errors. tagging follow-ups in the postmortem doc.

customer-success: sending notification to customers impacted with ETA for follow-up postmortem. will share once devon has artifact links.

incidents-bot: Incident declared resolved for customer-facing traffic after routing completed and error rates stabilized. Please create a postmortem ticket and include timeline, graphs, tcpdumps, and remediation plan.

maria: creating postmortem ticket now and assigning to devon. thanks everyone for quick coord.

aj: closing out on-call. leaving a brief runbook update: add automated detection on kernel rx/tx retransmit threshold and a safe fallback to reduce routing churn.

devon: will add host eviction automation + alert tweak. handwritten note: check NIC firmware / ENA driver versions as part of PM.

maria: handed off to devon. marking this thread for postmortem follow-up and customer comms. :white_check_mark:
